inspection found no new discrete defect, but CI attribution still blocks landing. | | **Proof confidence** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | The ordinary contributor-proof gate is exempt for this collaborator-authored PR; its body reports built-CLI model completion, Linux Gateway natural exit, and published-driver update checks, with historical and platform limits stated. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Product **Kind:** Bug fix · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** CLI and Gateway termination can stall or abandon cleanup, and the existing mitigation changes Node’s compiler defaults. **Reason:** The collaborator-authored direction approves replacing the workaround with existing lifecycle owners and explicitly records the remaining native-platform limitations. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Needs changes before merge - 1 item remains** Keep open: this maintainer-directed PR replaces main’s compiler workaround with owned natural shutdown; current-head CI remains blocked, and no new actionable defect was established in the inspected paths. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `a39a27b7f99c9d6b4e53dad9e924375bcd0b9387` ## Before merge - [ ] **Complete next step** - Account for every failed job in CI run 38106144930 with matching baseline evidence, repairing failures caused by this PR and qualifying inherited failures through the documented landing route. ## Findings None. ### Tests - Missing end-to-end proof: The supplied shipped-CLI and Linux Gateway observations are historical; native macOS and Windows qualification is expressly unclaimed.
Agent review details ### How this fits together CLI, Gateway, worker, and child-process lifecycle owners receive completion or cancellation requests and release accepted work, native resources, transports, and output before recording terminal outcomes. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[CLI or Gateway entry] --> B[Command lifecycle owner] B --> C[Accepted work and child transports] B --> D[Shutdown request] D --> E[Join work and native cleanup] C --> E E --> F[Record exit status] F --> G[Natural Node shutdown] ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Land the owned natural-shutdown cutover after current-head CI failures are repaired or qualify through the documented inherited-failure route. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? No reproduction was run during this read-only review; the merged predecessor records real Node deadlocks, while current main mitigates them by disabling the affected compilers. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Owned cleanup and natural termination address the lifecycle cause while preserving explicit compiler policy, signal outcomes, and system-certificate trust.
